item.title: Gear
item.description:
Gears are a critical mid-to-late-game craftable resource in Kittens Game, functioning as an integral component for buildings and upgrades that increase automation and industrial efficiency.

Production and Acquisition

  • Recipe: One Gear is crafted in the Workshop using 15 Steel.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research the Steel science technology to unlock Gear crafting.
  • Crafting Efficiency: Kittens with the Metallurgist trait provide a specific +0.1 bonus to your craftRatio for Gears when assigned as the village leader.

Primary Building Requirements

Gears are a mandatory material for constructing several industrial and resource-gathering structures:

Gears are a critical mid-to-late-game craftable resource in Kittens Game, functioning as an integral component for buildings and upgrades that increase automation and industrial efficiency.

Production and Acquisition

  • Recipe: One Gear is crafted in the Workshop using 15 Steel.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research the Steel science technology to unlock Gear crafting.
  • Crafting Efficiency: Kittens with the Metallurgist trait provide a specific +0.1 bonus to your craftRatio for Gears when assigned as the village leader.

Primary Building Requirements

Gears are a mandatory material for constructing several industrial and resource-gathering structures:

  • Steamworks: Requires 20 Gears.
  • Magnetos: Requires 5 Gears.
  • Oil Wells: Requires 25 Gears.

Key Workshop Upgrades

Gears are heavily utilized in the Workshop, particularly for upgrades that automate manual tasks or enhance industrial output:

  • Printing & Pressing: Upgrades like the Printing Press (45 Gears), Offset Press (250 Gears), and Photolithography (1,250 Gears) allow Steamworks to automatically generate manuscripts.
  • Industrial Automation: Workshop Automation (25 Gears) and Advanced Automation (75 Gears) enable Steamworks to automatically craft slabs and beams.
  • Production Boosts: Upgrades such as Steel Plants (750 Gears) and Rotary Kiln (500 Gears) improve the efficiency of Calciners.
  • Environmental & Efficiency: Carbon Sequestration (125 Gears) reduces factory pollution, while Robotic Assistance (10,000 Gears) significantly reduces kitten catnip consumption.

Strategic Importance

Gears represent the transition from manual resource management to automated industrial cycles. Because Gears are crafted from Steel (which is itself a refined resource), it is highly recommended to maximize your Workshops and Factories to achieve a high craft ratio. This ensures you produce multiple Gears for the same amount of Steel, which is vital for overcoming the “Theology hurdle” and establishing a robust industrial base.

item.title: Concrete
item.description:
Concrete is a critical mid-to-late-game craftable resource used primarily for advanced infrastructure, storage expansion, and space exploration. Its acquisition marks the beginning of the “Concrete Era,” which is a major milestone in a player’s first run.

Production and Unlocking

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Mechanization science technology (115K Science, 45 Blueprints) to unlock the ability to craft concrete and assign Engineers to automate its production.
  • Recipe: Crafting one unit of concrete requires 2,500 Slabs and 25 Steel.
  • Trait Bonus: Kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific bonus to crafting efficiency for concrete when assigned as a leader.

Major Upgrades

Concrete is essential for several Workshop upgrades that significantly boost village capacity:

Concrete is a critical mid-to-late-game craftable resource used primarily for advanced infrastructure, storage expansion, and space exploration. Its acquisition marks the beginning of the “Concrete Era,” which is a major milestone in a player’s first run.

Production and Unlocking

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Mechanization science technology (115K Science, 45 Blueprints) to unlock the ability to craft concrete and assign Engineers to automate its production.
  • Recipe: Crafting one unit of concrete requires 2,500 Slabs and 25 Steel.
  • Trait Bonus: Kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific bonus to crafting efficiency for concrete when assigned as a leader.

Major Upgrades

Concrete is essential for several Workshop upgrades that significantly boost village capacity:

  • Concrete Huts: Reduces the price ratio of Huts by 0.3 (30%), allowing for a much larger kitten population.
  • Concrete Pillars: Increases the maximum storage of wood, minerals, and iron in Barns and Warehouses by 5%, and gold/titanium by 5%.
  • Concrete Barns: Increases the storage capacity of Barns by 75%.
  • Concrete Warehouses: Increases the storage capacity of Warehouses by 35%.

Construction Uses

Many advanced buildings and space structures require concrete as a primary material:

  • Industrial/Science: Factories (15), Reactors (50), Accelerators (125), Hydro Plants (100), and Data Centers (10).
  • Space Infrastructure: Lunar Outposts (150), Moon Bases (250), and Cryostations (1,500).

Strategic Importance

The “Concrete Era” is often the target for a player’s first reset. Strategy guides generally recommend pushing until you can afford Concrete Huts and reach at least 130 kittens. This ensures you gain at least 60 Paragon, providing a substantial production and storage boost for your next run. To reach the 125K science cap required for Concrete Huts, players often research Biology to build Bio Labs.

item.title: Compendium
item.description:
A Compendium is a mid-game craftable resource that represents the “sum of all modern knowledge of catkind”. It is primarily used to expand your Science storage capacity, which is essential for unlocking late-game technologies and space missions.

Production and Costs

To craft a Compendium, you must first research the Philosophy technology.

  • Cost: 50 Manuscripts and 10,000 Science.
  • Crafting Efficiency: Like other workshop resources, the number of Compendiums produced per craft is significantly increased by your Workshop and Factory craft bonuses.
  • Metaphysics Bonus: The Codex Logos upgrade (50 Paragon) adds +25% to the craft ratio and provides a x1.1 multiplier to Compendium crafting.

Primary Effects

  • Science Storage: Each Compendium provides a permanent +10 bonus to your maximum Science cap.
  • Storage Cap: By default, the maximum bonus you can receive from Compendiums is capped at 100% of your total science storage from buildings.
    • In Iron Will mode, this cap is significantly higher (1000%).
    • Data Centres increase the “Compendium Cap” by 1,000 each.
    • The Uplink and Starlink workshop upgrades further increase this cap by +1% per Bio Lab.

Strategic Utility

Compendiums act as a bridge between the industrial era and the space era, where technology costs begin to exceed the storage limits of standard buildings.

Compendiums act as a bridge between the industrial era and the space era, where technology costs begin to exceed the storage limits of standard buildings.

  • Technological Gatekeeper: Compendiums are a required component for researching critical sciences, including:
    • Architecture (10 Compendiums)
    • Physics (35 Compendiums)
    • Chemistry (50 Compendiums)
    • Acoustics (60 Compendiums)
    • Geology (65 Compendiums)
    • Biology (100 Compendiums)
  • Grinding Blueprints: Compendiums are the raw material for crafting Blueprints (25,000 Science + 25 Compendiums), which are necessary for advanced industrial and space structures.
  • Chronosphere Resets: When resetting with Chronospheres, carrying over a large stockpile of Compendiums is vital. Because they preserve your science cap, you can immediately research expensive technologies in the next run without waiting to rebuild massive amounts of libraries and observatories.

Optimization Tip

To grind Compendiums efficiently, focus on maximizing your Culture and Catpower production first. This allows you to mass-produce Manuscripts, which are the primary bottleneck for Compendium crafting. Once your Science cap is full, use the “Craft All” function in the Workshop to convert those manuscripts into Compendiums.

item.title: Tanker
item.description:
A Tanker is a high-tier craftable resource in Kittens Game primarily used to expand your colony’s maximum Oil storage capacity. Each Tanker built provides a flat increase of +500 to the oil cap.

Tankers are unlocked by researching Robotics. Because they require a significant amount of materials, they are considered a relatively expensive method of increasing storage. The crafting cost for a single Tanker is:

  • 200 Trade Ships
  • 1250 Alloy
  • 5 Blueprints

While Tankers provide a reliable way to boost your oil limit, strategic guides offer specific warnings regarding their efficiency:
item.content:encoded:
A Tanker is a high-tier craftable resource in Kittens Game primarily used to expand your colony’s maximum Oil storage capacity. Each Tanker built provides a flat increase of +500 to the oil cap.

Acquisition and Cost

Tankers are unlocked by researching Robotics. Because they require a significant amount of materials, they are considered a relatively expensive method of increasing storage. The crafting cost for a single Tanker is:

  • 200 Trade Ships
  • 1250 Alloy
  • 5 Blueprints

Strategic Utility and Advice

While Tankers provide a reliable way to boost your oil limit, strategic guides offer specific warnings regarding their efficiency:

  • The Oil Well Alternative: In some stages of the game (specifically during the Iron Will 40k run), relying on Tankers to reach oil caps is often deemed suboptimal. It is generally recommended to focus on grinding out the Steel necessary to build more Oil Wells instead, as they are often more resource-effective for reaching cap requirements.
  • Automation: Once you have Engineers, you can assign them to automatically craft Tankers (as well as Kerosene) to prevent your oil from capping and production from halting while you are away from the game.

Preservation and Resets

As a crafted resource, Tankers are normally lost upon resetting the game. However, they can be preserved across runs if the player has:

  1. Chronospheres: At least one active Chronosphere.
  2. Flux Condensator: This workshop upgrade allows Chronospheres to carry over a portion of crafted resources, including Tankers.

The amount preserved is calculated as a fraction based on the number of Chronospheres and the square root of the quantity of Tankers possessed prior to the reset. This makes them vital for “Positive Resets” in the late game, where players aim to start a new run with high storage capacities already intact.

item.content:encoded:
Alloy is a crucial craftable resource in Kittens Game, marking a mid-to-late game phase of infrastructure development.

Resource Details

Alloy is a composite material refined from other metals and is categorised as a craftable resource.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Technology Chemistry, which itself requires Physics.
Crafting Cost 75 Steel and 10 Titanium.
Unlocks The crafting of Alloy is unlocked by the Chemistry technology.

Uses and Strategic Importance

Alloy is necessary for constructing advanced buildings, structures, and various Workshop upgrades:

  1. Buildings:
    • Bio Lab: Requires 25 Alloy and 100 Slab to build, significantly boosting Science production and storage.
    • Magneto: Requires 10 Alloy, 5 Gear, and 1 Blueprint to construct, providing a crucial +2% Global Production boost and generating 5 Energy.
  2. Workshop Upgrades: Alloy is the prerequisite material for several high-tier upgrades:
    • Alloy Saw: Requires Alloy and improves Lumber Mill efficiency by $+15%$.
    • Alloy Axe: Requires Alloy and makes Woodcutters $50%$ more effective.
    • Alloy Barns/Warehouses: Required for various storage upgrades.
    • Alloy Armour/Nanosuits: Required for advanced Hunting bonuses.

Progression in the “Alloy Era”

The point where Alloy becomes readily available signals a major checkpoint in the game’s progression.

  • Technology Path: Getting to the Alloy era requires a specific scientific path: Navigation $\to$ Physics $\to$ Chemistry.
  • Resource Bottlenecks: Alloy requires substantial amounts of Titanium, which must be acquired primarily through trading slabs with Zebras. This titanium requirement mandates ongoing construction of Trade Ships and Observatories (to acquire Starcharts).
  • Strategic Focus: Once Alloy is unlocked, strategic focus shifts to purchasing Alloy buildings and the associated upgrades to boost storage and production. The next major goal after the Alloy era is typically achieving Concrete Huts.
  • Trait Bonus: Kittens with the Metallurgist trait, when assigned as a leader, provide a specific bonus to metal crafting efficiency, increasing the craft ratio for resources including Alloy by $+0.1$.

Finally, Alloy is also a component, alongside Unobtainium, in crafting the late-game resource Eludium.

item.title: Bloodstone
item.description:
Bloodstone is classified as an uncommon resource in Kittens Game that plays a role in late-game crafting and unlocks specific buildings associated with the Zebras,. It is poetically described as a strange jewelry claimed to be made of time and a blood of elder gods.

Acquisition Methods

Bloodstone can be acquired through hunting and crafted using advanced resources:

  1. Hunting: Bloodstone has a chance to be found when engaging in hunting, provided you have at least 10 Zebras,. In the Iron Will challenge mode, the chance to yield a bloodstone during a hunt is 0.05% if you already have it. However, this chance increases significantly to 5% if you do not already have bloodstone.

  2. Crafting: Bloodstone is a craftable item unlocked by the Zebra Forge. The crafting cost is high, requiring temporal and elder resources: 5,000 Time Crystal and 10,000 Relic.

  • Zebra Outpost: Requires 1 Bloodstone.

Persistence

As a craftable resource, Bloodstone is retained across game resets, but only conditionally. It is carried over if the player has Chronospheres built and the Flux Condensator workshop upgrade researched. The amount carried over is subject to diminishing returns.

item.title: Steel
item.description:
Steel is a mid-game technology and a critical craftable resource in Kittens Game, marking a major step toward industrialization and advanced building construction.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Steel based on the sources:

Steel Technology

The technology named Steel has the following characteristics:

  • Prerequisite: It is unlocked after researching Writing.
  • Cost: Researching Steel requires 12,000 Science.
  • Strategic Timing: Steel is one of the three “specialist Techs” available after Writing (alongside Philosophy and Machinery). Strategic advice suggests researching Steel first among these three options to acquire useful upgrades that strengthen your economy.

Steel Resource (Crafting and Composition)

Steel is a Craftable Resource.
item.content:encoded:
Steel is a mid-game technology and a critical craftable resource in Kittens Game, marking a major step toward industrialization and advanced building construction.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Steel based on the sources:

Steel Technology

The technology named Steel has the following characteristics:

  • Prerequisite: It is unlocked after researching Writing.
  • Cost: Researching Steel requires 12,000 Science.
  • Strategic Timing: Steel is one of the three “specialist Techs” available after Writing (alongside Philosophy and Machinery). Strategic advice suggests researching Steel first among these three options to acquire useful upgrades that strengthen your economy.

Steel Resource (Crafting and Composition)

Steel is a Craftable Resource.

  • Composition: Steel is made by combining 100 Iron and 100 Coal.
  • Acquisition: The research of the Steel technology enables the resource Steel.
  • Trading: Steel can also be acquired through trade, notably from Griffins, who sell 25 Steel per trade once you reach Embassy Level 5. Griffins buy Wood.

Key Unlocks and Upgrades

Researching Steel unlocks critical Workshop Upgrades, many of which focus on resource efficiency and early Coal production:

Upgrade Name Cost Components (Examples) Primary Effect
Coal Furnace Science, Minerals, Iron, Beam Allows Smelters to produce 0.005 Coal per tick while burning wood.
Deep Mining Science, Iron, Beam Allows Mines to produce 0.003 Coal per tick.
Steel Axe Science, Steel Makes Woodcutters 50% more effective.
Reinforced Warehouses Science, Plate, Steel, Scaffold Increases resource storage in Warehouses, Barns, Harbours, and Mints by 25%.
Steel Armour Science, Steel Provides a +0.5 Hunting bonus.
Steel Saw Science, Steel Improves Lumber Mill efficiency by 20%.
High Pressure Engine Science, Gear, Blueprint Reduces Steamworks coal consumption by 20%.

Usage in Buildings and Crafting

Steel is crucial for moving beyond basic construction into industrial and specialized buildings:

  • Advanced Materials: Steel is required for crafting Gears.
  • Industrial Buildings:
    • The Steamworks building requires 65 Steel (along with 20 Gear and 1 Blueprint).
    • The Quarry building requires 125 Steel.
    • The Calciner building requires 100 Steel.
  • Housing: It is required for the mid-game Mansion building (75 Steel).
  • Crafting: Steel is a component of Concrete, which is crafted from 25 Steel and 2500 Slab.

Strategic Notes

  • Early Coal: Steel is essential because it unlocks the upgrades (Coal Furnace and Deep Mining) necessary to begin accumulating Coal. Coal is required to craft Steel itself, and to power industrial structures like the Steamworks.
  • Iron Priority: Once Steel is researched and the coal-producing upgrades are acquired, players are often advised to let Coal production max out. This is because the Iron used to produce Coal is highly valuable and better prioritized for building Lumber Mills and Observatories.
  • Trade Importance: Trading with Zebras yields Iron, which can then be converted into Steel. This trade route helps maintain a supply of Steel, especially once it becomes a bottleneck for future buildings.

item.title: Trade_Ship
item.description:
Trade Ships are a craftable resource in Kittens Game essential for enabling trade with other civilisations, particularly for acquiring late-game bottleneck resources like titanium.

Unlocking and Crafting

  • Prerequisite: Trade Ships are unlocked after researching Navigation science, which itself requires Astronomy (28K Science, 65 Manuscripts) and 100 Manuscripts to research.
  • Crafting Cost: Crafting a single Trade Ship requires:
    • 100 Scaffold
    • 150 Plate
    • 25 Starchart
  • Cost Reduction: The starchart requirement to craft Trade Ships can be reduced by the Satellite Navigation upgrade, offering a 1.25% discount per active Satellite, up to a maximum discount of 75%. At 45 Satellites, the cost reaches 10.9375 Starcharts, where diminishing returns begin.

Functionality and Strategic Importance

Trade Ships serve several critical roles in resource acquisition and infrastructure:
item.content:encoded:
Trade Ships are a craftable resource in Kittens Game essential for enabling trade with other civilisations, particularly for acquiring late-game bottleneck resources like titanium.

Unlocking and Crafting

  • Prerequisite: Trade Ships are unlocked after researching Navigation science, which itself requires Astronomy (28K Science, 65 Manuscripts) and 100 Manuscripts to research.
  • Crafting Cost: Crafting a single Trade Ship requires:
    • 100 Scaffold
    • 150 Plate
    • 25 Starchart
  • Cost Reduction: The starchart requirement to craft Trade Ships can be reduced by the Satellite Navigation upgrade, offering a 1.25% discount per active Satellite, up to a maximum discount of 75%. At 45 Satellites, the cost reaches 10.9375 Starcharts, where diminishing returns begin.

Functionality and Strategic Importance

Trade Ships serve several critical roles in resource acquisition and infrastructure:

  1. Enabling Exploration and Trade: Owning at least one Trade Ship is the prerequisite for discovering and trading with the Zebras.
  2. Acquisition of Titanium: Trade Ships are critical for solving the titanium bottleneck. Zebras sell Titanium in amounts determined by the number of Trade Ships you possess, via the formula (0.03 * Trade Ships) + 1.5. Importantly, this amount of titanium acquired is not affected by normal trading bonuses like those from Tradeposts.
  3. Storage Enhancement: Trade Ships enhance the storage capacity of Harbours through the Expanded Cargo Workshop upgrade. Each Trade Ship provides a +1% bonus to Harbour capacity, subject to diminishing returns past 168.75% and a maximum limit of 225%. This limit can be further increased by +5% per active Reactor if the Reactor Vessel upgrade is researched.
  4. Mid-Game Progression: Accumulating Trade Ships accelerates the titanium and iron acquisition necessary for constructing advanced buildings, such as Observatories. Due to the high iron requirement of Observatories, gaining titanium from Zebras allows you to stock up on resources needed to progress to the next technological tier.

Strategic Notes

  • Trade Ships are listed as a craftable resource that increases oil limit when crafted into a Tanker.
  • Starcharts are a significant bottleneck for this stage of the game, making the acquisition of Observatories—which increase the chance of astronomical events and subsequent starchart production—a high priority to sustain Trade Ship construction.
  • In the endgame, Trade Ships are sometimes ignored in favor of mints for Blueprint generation, but later become the fastest possible reset method when trading is used to acquire the blueprints needed for Chronospheres.

item.title: Kerosene Resource
item.description:
Kerosene is a high-tier craftable resource in Kittens Game that serves as the essential rocket fuel for late-game space exploration. It is produced by refining oil and is required to fund most space missions and construct advanced orbital infrastructure.

Acquisition and Cost

  • Unlocking: You must research the Oil Processing technology (215k Science, 150 Blueprints), which is available only after completing Rocketry.
  • Crafting Cost: Each unit of kerosene costs 7,500 oil.
  • Refinement Bonuses:
    • Factory Processing: This workshop upgrade (available via Oil Processing) increases the effectiveness of kerosene refinement by 5% per Factory.
    • Chemist Trait: Assigning a kitten with the Chemist trait as your Leader provides a +0.075 craft ratio bonus to kerosene production.

Primary Uses in Space

Kerosene is mandatory for nearly all activities beyond the initial orbital launch:
item.content:encoded:
Kerosene is a high-tier craftable resource in Kittens Game that serves as the essential rocket fuel for late-game space exploration. It is produced by refining oil and is required to fund most space missions and construct advanced orbital infrastructure.

Acquisition and Cost

  • Unlocking: You must research the Oil Processing technology (215k Science, 150 Blueprints), which is available only after completing Rocketry.
  • Crafting Cost: Each unit of kerosene costs 7,500 oil.
  • Refinement Bonuses:
    • Factory Processing: This workshop upgrade (available via Oil Processing) increases the effectiveness of kerosene refinement by 5% per Factory.
    • Chemist Trait: Assigning a kitten with the Chemist trait as your Leader provides a +0.075 craft ratio bonus to kerosene production.

Primary Uses in Space

Kerosene is mandatory for nearly all activities beyond the initial orbital launch:

  • Space Missions: It is required for missions to Dune (75 kerosene), Piscine (250), Helios (1,250), T-minus (750), Kairo (7,500), and beyond.
  • Orbital Structures: Large quantities are needed for high-tier buildings, most notably Space Beacons (7,500), Heatsinks (5,000), Terraforming Stations (5,000), and Sunlifters (2,500).
  • Infrastructure Upgrades: It is a required material for upgrading Warehouses into Spaceports (1,000 kerosene).

Strategic Management and Automation

Because oil production is often slow but kerosene requirements are massive, managing the oil-to-kerosene pipeline is a common late-game bottleneck.

  • Engineer Automation: Once you have Engineers, you can assign them to automatically craft kerosene. This is highly recommended to prevent oil from hitting its storage cap and halting production while you are away from the game.
  • Storage Requirements: To reach the 7,500 oil threshold for a single craft, you will likely need to build numerous Oil Wells or Tankers.

Preservation and Resets

As a crafted resource, kerosene is normally lost when you reset the game. However, it can be preserved across runs if you possess:

  1. Chronospheres: Each active sphere preserves a portion of your resources.
  2. Flux Condensator: This specific workshop upgrade (unlocked via Chronophysics) is required for Chronospheres to carry over crafted resources like kerosene.

The amount of kerosene saved is determined by the number of Chronospheres and the square root of your total kerosene at the time of reset. This preservation is essential for “Positive Resets,” allowing you to bypass the early-game oil grind and return to space immediately in a new run.

item.title: Eludium
item.description:
Eludium is an extremely rare and expensive high-tier crafted resource in Kittens Game, described as a composite of Unobtainium and Alloy.

  • Production Multipliers: The yield is significantly boosted by your overall Workshop craft ratio. Furthermore, kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific crafting bonus (+0.075) for eludium, and the Antimatter Fission workshop upgrade makes Engineers 25% more effective at producing it.

Strategic Infrastructure and Buildings

Eludium is a critical component for late-game population scaling and advanced industrial structures:
item.content:encoded:
Eludium is an extremely rare and expensive high-tier crafted resource in Kittens Game, described as a composite of Unobtainium and Alloy.

Acquisition and Production

  • Unlocking: Eludium is unlocked through the Exometallurgy science (formerly known as Advanced Exogeology).
  • Crafting Recipe: Crafting one unit of eludium requires 1,000 Unobtainium and 2,500 Alloy.
  • Production Multipliers: The yield is significantly boosted by your overall Workshop craft ratio. Furthermore, kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific crafting bonus (+0.075) for eludium, and the Antimatter Fission workshop upgrade makes Engineers 25% more effective at producing it.

Strategic Infrastructure and Buildings

Eludium is a critical component for late-game population scaling and advanced industrial structures:

  • Eludium Huts: This bonfire upgrade reduces the price ratio of Huts by 10%, allowing for much higher populations. While powerful, some strategic guides note that the 125 eludium cost may only provide a marginal (~1%) increase in paragon-per-hour efficiency in very short runs.
  • Cryostation: These supermassive storage facilities cost 25 eludium and are essential for reaching the high resource caps required for the deep endgame.
  • Spaceport: Eludium is required to build Spaceports, which enhance the capacity of other space structures like Moon Bases and Cryostations.
  • Sunlifter: Each Sunlifter costs 225 eludium and is the primary structure used to generate Antimatter.
  • Entanglement Station: These late-game structures require 5,000 eludium each and are used for quantum computing and reverse-engineering relics.

Workshop and Advanced Upgrades

Many high-tier upgrades are gated by eludium costs:

  • Eludium Reflectors: This upgrade increases your maximum Science capacity by +2% for every Observatory you own.
  • Microwarp Reactors: Costing 50 eludium, this is a vital upgrade that increases the Unobtainium production of Lunar Outposts by 75%.
  • Scientific Utility: It is required for several advanced workshop techs including Cryocomputing (Data Center efficiency), Machine Learning, Antimatter Reactors, and Chronoengineers.

Preservation and Reset Strategy

  • Preservation: Eludium is a crafted resource and can be carried over through game resets if you have Chronospheres and the Flux Condensator upgrade.
  • Diminishing Returns: The amount preserved follows a square root formula: $1.5* {number of Chronospheres}* sqrt(current eludium amount)$.
  • Efficiency Tipping Point: A common strategy for rapid resets is to stockpile 1,111 eludium before resetting with one Chronosphere. This ensures you start the next run with the 50 eludium needed to immediately purchase Microwarp Reactors and accelerate your Unobtainium production.

  • Trading: Manuscripts can be obtained through trade with the Sharks (15% chance) once you have an Embassy level of at least 10.

Automation and Scaling

The “Theology hurdle”—the period where you must grind manuscripts manually—is a notorious progression bottleneck. To overcome this, players typically rely on the Steamworks building for automated production:

  • Printing Press: This workshop upgrade allows Steamworks to automatically print 0.0025 manuscripts per second.
  • Offset Press: Increases Steamworks production to 0.01 per second.
  • Photolithography: Further boosts production to 0.04 per second.

Primary Uses

Manuscripts are mandatory for transitioning into the religious and celestial eras of the game:

  • Technology Requirements: They are required to research Theology (35), Astronomy (65), and Navigation (100).
  • Building Construction: Each Temple requires 10 manuscripts to build.
  • Resource Conversion: They are the base material for crafting Compendiums, requiring 50 manuscripts each.
  • Culture Boost: Owning manuscripts provides a minor bonus to your maximum culture cap, though this effect suffers from diminishing returns.

Strategic Advice

  • Grinding Tactic: Before automation is available, the most efficient way to acquire manuscripts is to assign all kittens to the Hunter job to mass-produce parchment, then wait for culture to max out before using the “craft all” manuscript button.
  • Metaphysics Synergy: The Codex Vox upgrade adds a +25% bonus to your craft ratio for manuscripts and provides a 1.05x multiplier to all manuscript crafting.
  • Religious Pivot: If you enact the Lizard Relations: [Priests] ( /job/priest/) policy, manuscripts will grant maximum faith instead of a portion of the maximum culture they usually provide.

item.title: Megalith
item.description:
Megaliths are a mid-to-late game craftable resource used primarily for the construction of megastructures and the advancement of the unicorn religion.

Acquisition and Crafting

  • Workshop Crafting: Once the prerequisite technologies are met, a single megalith can be crafted using 50 Slabs, 25 Beams, and 5 Plates.
  • Trading with Nagas: Megaliths can also be obtained through trade with the Nagas. This requires 500 Ivory per trade and has a 10% chance of yielding a megalith, provided the player has reached an Embassy level of 15.

Primary Use: Ziggurats

The most critical application of megaliths is building Ziggurats, which cost 50 Megaliths, 50 Scaffolds, and 1 Blueprint each.

Primary Use: Ziggurats

The most critical application of megaliths is building Ziggurats, which cost 50 Megaliths, 50 Scaffolds, and 1 Blueprint each.

  • Unlocks: Ziggurats are the gateway to the unicorn religion system, enabling the sacrifice of unicorns to obtain Unicorn Tears.
  • Culture Boost: Each Ziggurat provides a +8% increase to maximum culture.
  • Visibility: While unlocked by the Construction technology, the Ziggurat will not appear in the Bonfire tab until the player possesses approximately 5 Megaliths, 5 Scaffolds, and 1 Blueprint.

Endgame and Religious Structures

In the late game, megaliths are a mandatory component for advanced structures within the Cryptotheology and unicorn trees:

  • Sky Palace: 5 Megaliths.
  • Marker: 750 Megaliths.
  • Unicorn Graveyard: 1,000 Megaliths.
  • Unicorn Necropolis: 2,500 Megaliths.
  • Black Pyramid: 2,500 Megaliths.

Strategic Considerations

Strategic guides recommend building a significant number of Ziggurats (ideally 25–30) before heavily investing in unicorn sacrifices, as the number of tears received per sacrifice is directly determined by the total number of Ziggurats owned.

Persistence and Resets

As a crafted resource, megaliths are normally lost upon resetting the game. To carry them over into a new run, a player must have at least one Chronosphere and the Flux Condensator Workshop upgrade. The amount preserved follows a square root formula based on the total quantity held before the reset.

Primary Uses

Metal plates are mandatory for progressing into the “Titanium Era” and establishing advanced energy systems:

Acquisition and Crafting

Primary Uses

Parchment is a mandatory requirement for transitioning out of the early game and establishing a “cultural engine”:

  • Resource Conversion: It is the primary input for crafting Manuscripts. Each manuscript requires 25 parchment (reduced to 20 with the Tradition policy).
  • Building Construction: It is a required material for several essential structures:
    • Amphitheatres: 3 Parchment (essential for reducing unhappiness and generating early culture).
    • Chapels: 250 Parchment (the primary structure for generating faith).
    • Breweries: 375 Parchment (required for holding Festivals).
  • Scientific Research: A massive stockpile of 5,000 parchment is required to research Drama and Poetry, which enables the festival system.

Strategic Management

  • Early-Game Grind: Strategic guides recommend beginning to craft parchment as often as possible once the Workshop is unlocked, as you will need vast quantities for the “Theology hurdle”.
  • The “Hunter Dump” Strategy: To efficiently accumulate parchment before automation is available, players should temporarily reassign all kittens to the Hunter job. This allows you to mass-produce the furs necessary for a bulk parchment craft session.
  • Policy Synergy: Enacting the Tradition policy is highly recommended because it reduces the parchment cost for manuscripts and doubles their cultural effectiveness, significantly speeding up mid-game scientific progress.

Special Constraints

  • Pacifism Challenge: In this challenge, hunting is disabled. You cannot obtain furs, and therefore cannot craft parchment, until you build a Mint to generate a passive supply of luxury resources.
  • Iron Will: Since you lack kittens for standard jobs in this mode, your parchment supply depends entirely on the furs gathered by Zebras acting as passive hunters.
  • Persistence: As a crafted resource, parchment is lost upon resetting the game unless you possess Chronospheres and the Flux Condensator workshop upgrade.

item.title: Refine_Catnip

    • Bio Labs: Each lab increases catnip refinement effectiveness by 10%.

item.title: Scaffold

  • Discovery: Possessing at least one trade ship is the prerequisite for exploring and discovering the Zebras, the primary source of titanium through trade.
  • Harbours: Scaffolds are required to build Harbours (5 scaffolds each), which provide a massive boost to the storage capacity of multiple resources.

Thorium is central to scaling your energy grid and scientific capacity through several key Workshop upgrades:

  • Enriched Thorium: This vital efficiency upgrade reduces the Thorium consumption of your reactors by 0.0625 per tick, helping to stabilise your stockpiles.
  • Quantum Dot Cells: Costs 175k Science, 200 Eludium, and 1000 Thorium. It improves Solar Farm energy production by 15% in winter and 30% in spring and autumn.
  • Thorium Drive: A high-tier engine that divides space travel time by 50 (or 75 if combined with an Antimatter Drive).

Space Missions and Structures

As you progress into the late-game “Umbra” and “Centaurus” eras, Thorium becomes a mandatory requirement for exploration:

  • Missions: Significant quantities are required for missions to Umbra (15,000), Charon (35,000), Centaurus (50,000), and the Furthest Ring (75,000).
  • Heatsinks: Essential for increasing antimatter storage, each Heatsink costs 12,500 Thorium.
  • Tectonics: These space structures, which generate 25 Watts of energy, cost 75,000 Thorium each.

Strategic Utility

  • The Antimatter Seed: In long “seed runs” aimed at reaching a 5,000 antimatter capacity, Thorium is often a major bottleneck. Reaching the milestone of 34 Heatsinks requires over 526,000 Thorium.

  • Preservation: As a crafted resource, Thorium is normally lost upon resetting. To carry it over into a new run, you must possess Chronospheres and the Flux Condensator Workshop upgrade. The amount preserved is determined by the square root of your total Thorium at the time of reset.
